stories.title: Chinese Restaurant Chain to Open 10K-SF Eatery at 365 West 46th Street
stories.excerpt: One thing New York City does not lack is a place to find great Chinese food, and New Yorkers are about to get another spot to add to their lists. Nong Geng Ji, one of China’s most popular Hunan cuisine brands, has inked a 9,900-square-foot retail lease at 365 West 46th Street in Manhattan’s Hell’s Kitchen neighborhood along the famed Restaurant Row, according to tenant broker Meridian Capital Group. The three-level space will be the brand’s flagship New York City location. The length of the lease was not disclosed, but the asking rent is $55,000 per month, according to Meridian. James Famularo and Kyle Fink of Meridian represented the tenant, while Milly Cheung and Jordan Cohen from Lee & Associates NYC represented the landlord, Lucky 11 Group. “Restaurant Row is one of the most competitive dining corridors in Manhattan, and a three-level space of this size very rarely becomes available there,” Fink said in a statement. “Nong Geng Ji was looking for a location that could support the volume of a flagship while putting the brand in front of the Theater District audience every night.” Nong Geng Ji will replace sushi restaurant Sushi Seki in the space. Nong Geng Ji was founded in 2017 and has grown across China and around the world. The restaurant’s first New York City location — and its first U.S. location — opened earlier this year at 135-15 37th Avenue in Flushing, Queens. “The landlord chose this brand because it is well known in China, and the brand plans to add local flavors to its famous dishes to meet local needs,” Lee’s Cheung told Commercial Observer. “Our location is close to Times Square and the Theatre District. We want to bring authentic Chinese flavor to people not only in New York but from everywhere.” Located between Eighth and Ninth avenues, 365 West 46th Street is a four-story mixed-use property. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Nong Geng Ji (China's Hunan cuisine brand) leases 9,900 SF at 365 W. 46th St., Manhattan
Three-level flagship space in Hell's Kitchen on Restaurant Row at $55K/month asking rent
High-volume restaurant concept signals continued retail demand in Manhattan theater/hospitality corridor
stories.summary: Nong Geng Ji, a major Chinese restaurant chain, has signed a 9,900-square-foot lease for a three-level flagship location at 365 West 46th Street in Manhattan's Hell's Kitchen neighborhood along Restaurant Row. The space commands $55,000 per month in asking rent. The deal demonstrates sustained retail demand in a competitive Manhattan dining corridor, though the lease term was not disclosed.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact on multifamily development. Restaurant activation in Hell's Kitchen/Midtown West supports neighborhood vitality and can improve amenity appeal for residential projects in the submarket, but this is primarily a retail/hospitality signal, not a demand driver for apartment construction.

stories.title: World Trade Centers Association Leases 3K-SF Office in Namesake Campus
stories.excerpt: The international trade organization that took its name from the World Trade Center is re-establishing a headquarters presence at the campus. The World Trade Centers Association (WTCA), which bought the rights to the name in the 1980s, has signed a lease for 2,556 square feet on the 46th floor of the Durst Organization and the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey (PANYNJ)’s One World Trade Center after a 25-year absence, according to the organization. The length of the lease and the names of brokers on the deal were not disclosed, but the asking rent for the tower was in the ​​high $80s to $90s per square foot as of July, Commercial Observer reported at the time. “Returning our global headquarters to One World Trade Center is both a meaningful homecoming and a significant milestone for WTCA and our continued growth as a global organization,” John Drew, chair of the WTCA board of directors, said in a statement. “This new office space gives us a dynamic setting — and a fitting global address — to bring together members and partners from around the world as we continue building connections that support trade, investment and economic growth.” The WTCA bought the license to use the World Trade Center name from the PANYNJ for just $10 and has since been licensing it back out to PANYNJ and other organizations. But in 2013, it was reported that the WTCA was attempting to make a deal with owning private-public partnerships, allowing them to use the name free of charge in exchange for office space valued at $500,000 per year. WTCA, Durst and the PANYNJ did not immediately confirm whether any elements of this proposal made it into the framework of the current lease deal. At the time of the 2013 request by WTCA, PANYNJ officials expressed concern that another organization bought the trademark for such a low price and was later allegedly leveraging it to get a slice of what would be one of the most sought-after office properties in the country. &#822
bullets: World Trade Centers Association leases 2,556 SF on 46th floor of One World Trade Center
WTCA returns global HQ to WTC campus after 25-year absence; asking rent in high $80s–$90s/SF
Office re-tenanting at iconic lower Manhattan asset; no lease term or broker details disclosed
stories.summary: The World Trade Centers Association has signed a lease for 2,556 square feet on the 46th floor of One World Trade Center, marking its return to the WTC campus after 25 years. The asking rent was in the high $80s to $90s per square foot as of July. The organization described the move as both a homecoming and a significant milestone for continued global growth.
stories.impact: Nominal impact on multifamily. Office leasing activity in lower Manhattan is a weak signal—the market remains challenged by hybrid work and rising vacancies. A symbolic 2.5K-SF anchor tenant does not shift residential demand fundamentals in downtown Manhattan or nearby neighborhoods like Battery Park City or the Financial District.

stories.title: 100K-SF MOB Portfolio Changes Hands in Phoenix
stories.excerpt: A three-building, 98,500-square-foot medical office portfolio in the Phoenix Metro area sold for $12.8 million. The properties were sold by Evernorth Care Group (formerly operated as Cigna Medical Group). MCR Companies, completing a 1031 exchange, acquired the properties in Glendale and Chandler. A Phoenix Property was purchased by Empower College Prep. The portfolio consists of the following properties:• 5891 W. Eugie Ave in Glendale – a 35,000 square foot, two-story medical office building• 2302 N. 75th Ave in Phoenix – a 44,000 square foot, two-story medical office building• 1717 W. Chandler Blvd in Chandler — an 18,600 square foot, single-story medical office buildingAll three buildings are positioned near flagship health system campuses in their respective submarkets: Banner Thunderbird Medical Center in Glendale, Banner Estrella Medical Center in Phoenix, and Dignity Health Chandler Regional Medical Center in Chandler.Geoffrey Turbow, Emily Minnier, Brian Butler and W. Glenn Dyke of CBRE represented the seller in the three transactions. The post 100K-SF MOB Portfolio Changes Hands in Phoenix appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MCR Companies acquires 98,500 SF medical office portfolio (3 buildings) in Phoenix/Glendale/Chandler for $12.8M
Evernorth Care Group divests; MCR executing 1031 exchange; buildings positioned near major health campuses
Medical office portfolio sale; reflects healthcare real estate liquidity but no direct multifamily signal
stories.summary: MCR Companies has acquired a three-building, 98,500-square-foot medical office portfolio in the Phoenix metro area (Glendale, Phoenix, and Chandler) for $12.8 million from Evernorth Care Group via 1031 exchange. The properties total 35K, 44K, and 18.6K square feet respectively and are strategically positioned near Banner and Dignity Health flagship medical centers. One Phoenix property was separately purchased by Empower College Prep.
stories.impact: Indirect multifamily relevance in Phoenix submarkets. Healthcare system investments and MOB activity near major campuses (Banner Thunderbird, Banner Estrella, Dignity Health Chandler) indicate continued employer/institutional presence and job stability. This supports long-term multifamily demand anchors in these submarkets, but the sale itself is a distressed/portfolio liquidation, not a growth signal.

stories.title: Equus Trades Tucson Warehouse Portfolio for $165.7M
stories.excerpt: Everview Partners purchased an 85-building, 1.25 million square foot shallow bay industrial portfolio across Tucson for $165.75 million. The portfolio was roughly 90 percent leased to 452 tenants at the time of sale. The portfolio spanned 14 properties. The seller, Pegasus Tucson Owner LLC of Newtown Square, PA, is associated with Equus Capital Partners. Real Estate Daily News reports that the properties were originally acquired by Equus-sponsored funds in October 2021 for approximately $150 million. Will Strong, Michael Matchett, Madeline Warren, Molly Miller and Jack Stamets with Cushman & Wakefield’s National Industrial Advisory Group, together with Paul Hooker of Cushman & Wakefield | PICOR in Tucson, represented both the buyer and seller. The properties provide a mix of warehouse, office and flex space for businesses throughout the Tucson market. Their locations span several established industrial and employment corridors, including Forbes Boulevard, Prince Road, Ruthrauff Road, Palo Verde Road, Research Loop, Dodge Boulevard, Speedway Boulevard and East 29th Street. The post Equus Trades Tucson Warehouse Portfolio for $165.7M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Everview Partners buys 85-building, 1.25M SF shallow-bay industrial portfolio in Tucson for $165.75M
Portfolio 90% leased to 452 tenants; seller (Equus Capital Partners) held since Oct. 2021 (~$150M acquisition)
Strong industrial leasing fundamentals; ~$16.75M gain over 3+ years; portfolio spans 14 properties across 8+ corridors
stories.summary: Everview Partners purchased an 85-building, 1.25 million square foot shallow-bay industrial portfolio across Tucson for $165.75 million. The portfolio was roughly 90 percent leased to 452 tenants at the time of sale and spanned 14 locations across eight established industrial corridors. Seller Pegasus Tucson Owner LLC (affiliated with Equus Capital Partners) had acquired the properties in October 2021 for approximately $150 million.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Tucson industrial market strength reflects steady small-tenant logistics and light manufacturing demand, supporting regional economic stability. However, shallow-bay industrial portfolios do not drive residential in-migration or rent growth; Tucson multifamily demand remains tied to broader Sun Belt migration and job creation, not light industrial leasing activity.

stories.title: MCB Picks Up 421K-SF Laredo Logistics Facility
stories.excerpt: MCB Real Estate acquired Pinnacle One, a newly constructed 421,182-square-foot Class A industrial cross-dock facility located at 1401 Nicolas D. Hachar Road in Laredo, Texas. MCB Real Estate partnered with Vinecrest Capital as the Co-GP for the transaction. The project was built by Pure Development in 2024. The property is fully leased to Source Logistics. Source Logistics operates across 25 national locations and utilizes the Pinnacle One location to service its global clients. Pinnacle One sits on 25.82 acres. The property features 3,680 square feet of office space, 32-foot ceilings, 109 dock-high doors, four drive-in ramps, 173 trailer parking spaces, and 206 car spaces. It’s positioned just six miles from the World Trade Bridge and 18 miles from the Colombia Bridge. Laredo is the top trading port in the United States by dollar value, handling $236.2 billion in trade through July 2026. The post MCB Picks Up 421K-SF Laredo Logistics Facility appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: MCB Real Estate, partnering with Vinecrest Capital as co-GP, acquired Pinnacle One, a newly constructed 421,182-square-foot Class A industrial cross-dock facility in Laredo, Texas. Built in 2024 and fully leased to Source Logistics, the property sits on 25.82 acres with 109 dock-high doors, 32-foot ceilings, and is positioned six miles from the World Trade Bridge. Laredo is the top U.S. trading port by dollar value, handling $236.2 billion in trade.
stories.impact: Strong indirect signal for Laredo multifamily development. Logistics infrastructure investment and full-lease commitment to a major cross-dock facility underscore Laredo's strategic role in U.S.–Mexico trade and supply-chain operations. This attracts logistics operators and associated service-sector workers, supporting multifamily demand in Laredo's core and emerging submarkets; competitive positioning for build-to-suit and market-rate apartments tied to trade/logistics employment growth.

stories.title: Waterstone Acquires 660K-SF Matthews Retail Center
stories.excerpt: Waterstone Properties has paid $87 million for Windsor Square Shopping Center, a 659,222-square-foot power center in Matthews, N.C. Commercial Edge reports United Bank originated a $63.1 million acquisition loan. Hackney Real Estate Partners sold the asset after nearly two years of ownership. The firm had acquired Windsor Square from Sterling Organization for $70.1 million in November 2024. Completed in 1987, Windsor Square was most recently renovated in 2014. Anchored by national retailers including Kohl’s, At Home, Sam’s Club, Ross Dress for Less, PetSmart and DSW, among others, the asset was 99 percent leased at the time of sale. Atlantic Retail will handle leasing at the shopping center going forward. The shopping center is close to Novant Health Matthews Medical Center along the U.S. 74 retail corridor, providing direct access to Interstate 485. Downtown Charlotte is 11 miles away, while its international airport is some 30 miles northwest. The post Waterstone Acquires 660K-SF Matthews Retail Center appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Waterstone Properties paid $87 million for Windsor Square Shopping Center, a 659,222-square-foot power center in Matthews, North Carolina. The asset is 99 percent leased and anchored by national retailers including Kohl's, At Home, Sam's Club, Ross Dress for Less, PetSmart, and DSW. United Bank originated a $63.1 million acquisition loan. Seller Hackney Real Estate Partners had acquired the property from Sterling Organization for $70.1 million in November 2024.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Matthews is a suburban Charlotte submarket with strong retail anchors and proximal healthcare (Novant Health Matthews Medical Center). Retail power-center activity signals consumer spend and anchor-tenant stability but does not drive multifamily demand. Charlotte metro multifamily growth is driven by job creation (finance, tech, manufacturing) and migration, not retail leasing cycles.

stories.title: AI Office Demand Rises 27% Year-Over-Year
stories.excerpt: The number of new AI office leasing requirements rose 27% over the past year, from 644 to 820, VTS reported. Twelve of the 17 markets VTS tracks contributed to that growth. Most of the demand is concentrated in three markets: San Francisco, New York and Silicon Valley. Combined, they account for 64% of the 16.9 million square feet of active AI demand, and they hold 55 of the 83 large (50,000-plus square feet) requirements nationwide. Within this group, New York has moved into second place, according to VTS. Its 2.79 million square feet of active AI demand edges out Silicon Valley’s 2.78 million square feet, and it now has more large requirements than Silicon Valley, 18 to 16. Austin ranks fourth for active AI office demand with 1.25 million square feet, followed by Dallas-Fort Worth at 769,000 square feet. Growth is uneven across smaller markets. Some are surging from lower bases, including the San Francisco East Bay (up 130%), Washington, DC (up 94%) and Northern Virginia (up 50%). Others are pulling back, including Houston (down 54%), Atlanta and Seattle Eastside (each down 36%) and Denver (down 16%). The post AI Office Demand Rises 27% Year-Over-Year appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: AI office leasing demand rose 27% YoY (644 to 820 requirements); 16.9M SF active AI demand tracked
San Francisco, NYC, Silicon Valley dominate: 64% of active demand, 55 of 83 large (50K+) requirements
NYC moved to #2 (2.79M SF vs. Silicon Valley's 2.78M); Austin #4 (1.25M SF); Austin/DC/Northern VA surging; Houston/Atlanta/Seattle down 36–54%
stories.summary: AI office leasing demand has grown 27 percent year-over-year across tracked markets, rising from 644 to 820 new requirements and totaling 16.9 million square feet of active demand. Three markets—San Francisco, New York City, and Silicon Valley—account for 64 percent of active AI office requirements and 55 of 83 large (50,000-plus square feet) deals nationwide. New York has moved into second place with 2.79 million square feet of active AI demand, edging out Silicon Valley's 2.78 million. Austin ranks fourth with 1.25 million square feet, and Dallas-Fort Worth fifth with 769,000 square feet. Growth is uneven: San Francisco East Bay, Washington DC, and Northern Virginia are surging, while Houston, Atlanta, and Seattle are retreating.
stories.impact: Major demand signal for multifamily in AI-hub markets. NYC's surge into #2 office demand (beating Silicon Valley) reflects high-wage tech talent influx and signifies sustained residential demand in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Queens, and emerging tech neighborhoods. Austin's strong ranking (1.25M SF, #4 nationally) drives apartment demand well ahead of supply—underwriting premium rents in tech-proximate East Austin, South Congress, and Domain submarkets. Conversely, Houston/Atlanta/Seattle pullbacks suggest softening multifamily tailwinds in those metros; recalibrate underwriting and cap-rate assumptions downward for office-dependent markets.

stories.title: Stockbridge Buys Maryland Industrial Property for $57M
stories.excerpt: Stockbridge has acquired a 203,000-square-foot industrial property in Maryland for $56.6 million, almost four years after seller TA Realty bought the facility for about the same price. The San Francisco-based investment management firm purchased the Class A building at 8511 Pepco Place in Upper Marlboro, Md., according to Cushman & Wakefield, which represented the seller. CoStar first reported the news. The 13-acre property is fully leased to Harris Company, a mechanical contractor that has become a major service provider to hyperscale data center operators. Harris first occupied about 34 percent of the building before recently expanding to fill the entire space. The facility was built in 2008 about half a mile east of the Capital Beltway and near Joint Base Andrews. It includes a 190-foot truck court, 26 dock doors, two drive-in doors, 218 parking spaces and roughly 75 trailer spots. TA Realty acquired the asset from an affiliate of electrical distributor Sonepar in 2022 for $56.2 million. Harris’ expansion comes as Greater Washington’s data center industry drives demand for industrial space tied to construction, infrastructure and operations. Cushman & Wakefield’s Jonathan Carpenter, Graham Savage, Dawes Milchling and James Check worked on the transaction. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Stockbridge acquires 203,000 SF industrial property in Upper Marlboro, MD for $56.6M; fully leased to Harris Company
Harris Company (mechanical contractor/data-center service provider) expanded from 34% to 100% occupancy; TA Realty held ~4 years

stories.summary: Stockbridge has acquired a 203,000-square-foot Class A industrial property at 8511 Pepco Place in Upper Marlboro, Maryland for $56.6 million. The fully leased facility is occupied by Harris Company, a mechanical contractor that serves hyperscale data center operators and has recently expanded to occupy the entire building from an initial 34 percent. Built in 2008 on 13 acres, the property features a 190-foot truck court, 26 dock doors, 218 parking spaces, and approximately 75 trailer spots. Seller TA Realty had acquired the asset in 2022 for $56.2 million.
stories.impact: Indirect multifamily signal in Northern Virginia/DC suburbs. Harris Company's full-building expansion signals robust demand from hyperscale data center operators (AWS, Microsoft, Google) expanding in Northern Virginia/Dulles corridor. This inflates logistics and support-services employment in Upper Marlboro, Ashburn, and surrounding Maryland/DC suburbs, supporting multifamily demand for blue-collar and service-sector workers. However, the specific geographic submarket (Upper Marlboro) is not a prime multifamily hub; broader DC-area apartment demand is driven by federal/tech employment and immigration, not individual industrial leases.

stories.title: Inside Ken Griffin’s $3B Bet on Miami’s Wynwood
stories.excerpt: Three years ago, staffers working for billionaire financier Ken Griffin met with Moishe Mana to present him the deal of lifetime: They offered about $800 million for his 35-acre portfolio in Miami’s Wynwood neighborhood. Surprised, Mana initially rejected the offer. His properties were not for sale, and he envisioned developing his own business and entertainment district. But three days later, the investor relented. “Once I understood that this is going to be good for Miami,” Mana explained at a press event Thursday. “It’s completing our vision, not competing. I said, ‘Let’s go.’” The cash deal, which ultimately ballooned to $1.1 billion, closed this week without any outside debt and partners for Griffin. It marked one of the largest commercial real estate transactions in the country’s history. What’s more: Griffin pledged an additional $2 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, bringing his total giving to $3 billion — the largest combined donation to higher education from a private individual. $1 billion of the gift will support the university’s Pittsburgh campus, while $2 billion will support the launch of CMU Miami and includes the value of the real estate. The gift will help address one of Miami’s biggest challenges as it seeks to become a global business hub: its lack of top-tier universities, which are crucial to create a pipeline of employable grads for tech and finance companies. “If you look at Pittsburgh and the economic renaissance taking place: 250 tech startups, 100 companies focused on robotics,” Griffin said during a public address Thursday. “The future of America is being built in Pittsburgh — that future will be strengthened by what we build in Miami.” The Wynwood campus is expected to house more than 3,500 undergraduates, master’s, and PhD students as well as nearly 300 faculty members, and more than 600 staff. Griffin pledges additional $2B to Carnegie Mellon University (total $3B giving); one of largest U.S. CRE transactions ever

stories.summary: Billionaire Ken Griffin has closed a $1.1 billion all-cash acquisition of Moishe Mana's 35-acre portfolio in Miami's Wynwood neighborhood, one of the largest commercial real estate transactions in U.S. history. Mana initially rejected a proposed $800 million offer three years ago but ultimately agreed when convinced the investment would enhance his original vision. Separately, Griffin pledged $2 billion to Carnegie Mellon University, bringing his total educational giving to $3 billion. The Wynwood deal closed this week without external debt or partners.
stories.impact: Major multifamily demand catalyst in Miami's Wynwood submarket. Griffin's $1.1B+ commitment to a 35-acre urban infill portfolio signals intent to develop a large-scale mixed-use district (likely including residential, office, retail, hospitality). Wynwood's gentrification trajectory, artist community, and walkability appeal will support luxury-leaning and lifestyle-oriented multifamily. This acquisition may trigger competitive interest from other developers and capital in Miami's urban core; expect land values and construction costs to rise in Wynwood and adjacent neighborhoods (Allapattah, Buena Vista). Monitor Griffin's design/entitlement process for timing signals on multifamily delivery and absorption dynamics.

stories.title: Malaysian Bank, Medical Practice Sign Leases at 575 Madison Avenue
stories.excerpt: A Malaysian bank and a concierge medical service together took more than 14,100 square feet of office space in Midtown. Malayan Banking Berhad, also known as Maybank, signed the largest of the two deals with 8,629 square feet across the entire 24th floor of Steinberg & Pokoik Management’s 575 Madison Avenue, according to landlord broker CBRE. CBRE did not disclose the asking rent, but the average asking rent for office space in Midtown in the third quarter of 2026 was $85.08 per square foot, according to a report from Colliers. Maybank will relocate its New York City offices from 400 Park Avenue about three blocks away. Meanwhile, the smaller of the two deals was for Park 55 Medical Associates, where Dr. Wendy Ziecheck and Dr. Christopher Barley will practice medicine. Park 55 leased 5,474 square feet on part of the 10th and 15th floors of the building. “575 Madison Avenue attracts leading financial services and professional services tenants seeking a prestigious address and exceptional building amenities,” CBRE’s Gregg Rothkin said in a statement. “These latest transactions underscore the demand for high-quality office space in a premier Midtown location.” Rothkin negotiated on behalf of the landlord alongside CBRE’s David Hollander, Brad Auerbach, Maxwell Tarter and William Hooks, but it’s unclear who represented the tenants in the deals. In a third deal, another concierge health clinic, which CBRE declined to identify, leased 14,211 square feet at 575 Madison, according to the brokerage. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Maybank (Malaysian banking group) leases 8,629 SF (24th floor) at 575 Madison Avenue, Midtown Manhattan
Park 55 Medical Associates leases 5,474 SF on 10th & 15th floors; Maybank relocates from 400 Park Avenue (3 blocks away)
Combined 14,100+ SF signed; Midtown average asking rent Q3 2026: $85.08/SF; no lease terms/rates disclosed for these deals
stories.summary: Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank) has signed the largest of two office leases at 575 Madison Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, taking 8,629 square feet across the entire 24th floor. The Malaysian bank is relocating from 400 Park Avenue, three blocks away. Park 55 Medical Associates, a concierge medical practice operated by Dr. Wendy Ziecheck and Dr. Christopher Barley, leased 5,474 square feet on portions of the 10th and 15th floors. Combined, the two deals total over 14,100 square feet. Midtown Manhattan's average office asking rent in Q3 2026 was $85.08 per square foot.
stories.impact: Weak signal for Manhattan multifamily. Office leasing in Midtown is still below historical levels and reflects selective tenant activity in trophy properties (575 Madison is a prestigious address). International bank relocation across Midtown and medical practice expansion do not signal robust office demand recovery; multifamily demand in Manhattan remains driven by tech/finance employment and immigration, not tertiary office leasing. The submarket's residential value hinges on overall Manhattan job growth and housing supply scarcity, not individual office deals.
